translations.text: The Conversion of Kartli
Chapter 1. In the beginning, when King Alexander drove away the peoples of the sons of Lot and confined them in the land of Kedar,
he saw fierce peoples, the Bun-Turks, settled along the river Mtkvari in four cities, with their villages:
the city of Sarkine, Kaspi, Urbnisi and Odzrakhe, and their fortresses: the great fortress of Sarkine, Uplistsikhe of Kaspi, and the fortresses of Urbnisi and Odzrakhe.
Alexander was amazed, and he learned that they were of the race of the Jebusites. They ate every kind of flesh and had no graves; they ate their dead.
and the king could not fight them and went away. Then warlike peoples came, driven out from among the Chaldeans: the Huns,
and they asked the lord of the Bun-Turks for land in return for tribute, and they settled in Zanavi. And the place that they held in return for tribute is called Kherki.
And after some time Alexander, king of all the earth, came and destroyed these three cities and fortresses, and put the Huns to the sword.
But he fought against the city of Sarkine for eleven months. He camped on the west side of Sarkine, planted a vineyard, and brought a canal out from the Ksani,
And he settled men, Meruvians [?], with a dastag [?] of the river; and that place is called Nastagisi. And then he took Sarkine.
They themselves abandoned it and became fugitives. And King Alexander had with him Azo, son of the king of Arian-Kartli,
and he gave him Mtskheta as his seat and set his borders at Hereti, the Egrisi river, Armenia and the mountain of Tsroli. Then he departed.
and this Azo went to Arian-Kartli, to his father, and brought back eight houses and ten houses of foster-fathers,
and he settled in Old Mtskheta, and they had with them idols as gods: Gatsi and Ga. 1. And this Azo, son of the king of the Arian-Kartvelians, was the first king in Mtskheta, and he died.
2. And after him Pharnavaz was established. He erected a great idol on Tskhiri [?], and gave it the name Armazi.
And he built a wall on the side toward the water, and it is called Armazi. 3. And after him Saurmag became king.
He erected the idol Ainina on the road, and began building at Armazi. 4. And after him Mirvan reigned.
And he erected Danina on the road, further ahead, and built up Armazi. 5. And Pharnajob reigned and erected the idol Zaden on a mountain.
And he built a fortress. 6. And Arsok reigned and surrounded the city with walls. 7. And Arik reigned, who built the inner fortress at Armazi.
8. And Bratman reigned, in whose time the city at Mtskheta was begun. 9. And Mirian reigned.
And he built the city of Mtskheta. 10. And Arsuk reigned, who seized Kaspi and organized Uplistsikhe. 11.
And Rok reigned, who entirely [?] separated Mtskheta from himself. And the kingdom was divided in two, and two kings sat, one on that side and one on this side.
12. And Kardzam reigned at Armazi, and Bratman at Mtskheta. And in their times Jews came to Mtskheta and settled.
13. And on that side Pharsman reigned, and on this side Kaoz. 14. And on that side Arsok reigned, and on this side Amazaer. 15.
And on that side Amazasp reigned, and on this side Deruk. 16. And on that side Pharsman the Good reigned, and on this side Pharsman Avaz. 17.
And on that side Rok reigned, and on this side Mirdat. And in his time royal Armazi declined, and the kingship was in Mtskheta alone. 18.
And Ghadami reigned, and day 20 [?]. 19. And Pharsman. 20. And Amazasp. 21. And Rev the Just. 22. Vache. 23. Bakur. 24.
Mirdat. 25. Aspagur. 26. Lev, father of Mirian. 27. Mirian. These were the twenty-eight pagan kings in Kartli.
In the days of King Constantine, in the three hundred and tenth year after the Ascension of Christ, enemies made war, and they were badly beating King Constantine, son of Constantius.
And Emperor Constantine was preoccupied [?] with worries. There was a certain man of Ephesus, and he declared before the king:
"Those Christians, the Romans and all the Indians, and whoever holds that new law of holy Christ, mightily defeat their enemies by the wood of the Cross and by hope in it."
At that time the king set out with his troops, and he sent to bring bishops from Jerusalem, Antioch, Rome and Alexandria; and he himself and his mother were baptized together with the camp.
In the tenth year after that time Helena went to Jerusalem to search for the precious Cross.
And in the fourteenth year a certain woman of royal birth, named Rhipsime, fled for some reason, together with her foster-mother.
And there was with him a captive, a beautiful woman named Nino, whose story Queen Helena inquired into.
And she was a Roman noblewoman, and she had traveled her own way and had performed healings. And she had reached the land of the Greeks and was teaching that noblewoman Rhipsime.
And when Rhipsime fled toward the sea, Gaiane and Nino and some others with them came out into the regions of Armenia, the dwelling place of King Trdat. And they were martyred there.
But Nino remained, and she set out toward the mountains of the north and came to the river Mtkvari. She followed it and came to Mtskheta, the great city, the seat of the kings.
And she stayed like this for three years. She prayed in secret in a place covered with bramble thickets.
And she made the figure of a cross out of vine cuttings, and she stayed there and prayed. And that place was outside the city wall.
And that place of the brambles is the site of the altar of the upper church.
And in the fourth year she began to proclaim Christ God and his law: "And I found this northern land in error."
And in the sixth year she brought Nana, the king's wife, to faith during her illness, and in the seventh year she brought the king to faith through a miracle from Christ.
And she quickly built the lower church in the garden. And that pillar, which raised itself up, was made of wood.
And when they had built the church, an envoy was sent with a letter from Nino to the land of the Greeks, to King Constantine, to ask for priests. And they arrived quickly.
And the king gave Bishop John, two priests and one deacon, together with a letter from Queen Helena, an icon of the Saviour, and the wood of life for Nino.
And when they came, King Mirian, the queen and their whole household received baptism. They asked for wood to make a cross.
The carpenters searched and found a tree standing on a rocky hill. Its leaves never fell.
The tree was fragrant and very beautiful, as if clothed with the grace of Christ. The hill where it stood could not be reached because of the rock.
And they told the king and the bishop. And the king sent his son Rev and the archdeacon, and they saw how beautifully that tree stood.
And it was in leaf in the times of [?]. And the archdeacon recited the verse of David, saying:
"This tree is planted beside the outflow of the rock, watered by dew from on high, and its leaves will not fall forever." And he commanded the carpenters to cut down that tree.
And they made the form of the precious cross as the archdeacon taught. They made three crosses from the trunk of that tree, as three bodies, and erected them in Mtskheta,
As it is written in that small, briefly composed book of the Conversion of Kartli, written down by Gregory the deacon.
And King Mirian erected one cross on the mountain of Maghnari, which is called Tkhoti, and the other one near the Precious Cross itself.
And King Mirian sent and asked for stonecutters and lime masons from the land of the Greeks.
The king gave them, and they came to Erusheti. They laid the foundation of the church.
And they left the footboards of Jesus Christ, and they came to Manglisi and laid the foundation of a church and left the nails, and in this way they came to Mtskheta.
And the king began to build the church of the suburb in stone.
And when the king learned that they had first laid foundations in Erusheti and Manglisi and had left there those longed-for boards and nails,
he was filled with grief and halted the urgent work, until he learned from the archbishop:
"With you in this city is the garment of Christ, woven entirely from above, which those who crucified him divided among themselves,
and that tunic fell by lot to these people, and they hid it in this northern city. And now their children are here; who knows whether they may even know the place.
But its time is yet to come, when it will appear in glory upon the earth. Likewise the mantle of Elijah is also buried here."
And the king was filled with joy and at once summoned all the Jews and asked them: "Is it true?" And they declared the truth and did not deny it.
And they said: "From here went Elioz of Mtskheta and Longinus of Kanisi, and Talena and Misael."
And about the tunic, they said it had fallen to them by lot, but they denied knowing the place. Then King Mirian rejoiced when he learned that:
"Christ's tunic had first arrived at Mtskheta from Jerusalem." He gave thanks to God and said:
"Blessed are you, Lord Jesus Christ, Son of the living God, for you already desired our salvation beforehand, and our deliverance from the devil and from that place of darkness,
when you brought your garment through those Hebrews from the holy city of Jerusalem to the city of these foreign peoples, for at the time of your crucifixion our fathers were reigning in this city."
And the king and all Kartli advanced toward Christianity with great zeal. Then that blessed woman Nino said:
"Blessed is the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who sent his holy Word from the high heavens, from the mighty throne itself,
who came down to the lowly earth to be born in the flesh, without doubt, of the seed of David, from a woman, 'born alone' [?], holy and immaculate,
which was pleasing to him. By this means he brought about our life, enlightened all that is under heaven, and above all saved those who believe in him. For he was born as a man,
was honoured as God, and was baptized like some servant of the law, from water and earth [?]. But from above he was testified to and glorified by the Father and the Holy Spirit.
He was crucified, was buried and rose again. He ascended to those same heights with the Father and is coming in glory. To him praise is fitting. Amen."
When she had said this, she took with her Jacob the priest, who had come from Greece, and one eristavi (ruler of a province). She went and stayed at Tsobeni.
She summoned the mountaineers, the Chartalians, the Pkhovians and the Tsilkanians, and preached the faith of Christ to them.
But they refused, and the eristavi drew his sword a little. Out of fear they handed over their idols to be smashed.
And he crossed over to Ertso and stayed at Zhaleti, in the village of Edem, and baptized the people of Ertso-Tianeti.
The people of Kvareli heard of this and fled across to Tosheti [?]. They were found later, and King Trdat brought them and baptized them.
And Nino went down to Kkhoeti (!) and stayed at Katsareti, and she baptized the people of Kkhoeti (!) and the Sojni together with their folk.
She went over to Kakheti and stayed at Ktseli-daba. She brought the princes of Kakheti and baptized them.
And she fell ill and set out for Mtskheta. And when she reached Kkhoeti (!), the village called Bodini, she could go no farther.
And there came [?] from the city of Ujarma Rev, the king's son, and Salome, his wife,
And her daughter and [?] stood by her as caretakers, and the king and his wife Nana sent Archbishop John from Mtskheta to see her and bring her back.
But she did not wish this; instead she commended to him Jacob the priest: "so that after you he may hold the see."

And in his presence she handed over the letter written by Queen Helena, which had been written to Nino. In it the queen, by her royal authority, had honoured her as apostle and evangelist. She had also sent the wood of life to Queen Nana.
And John celebrated the liturgy and gave Nino communion of the body and blood of Christ. She took this as provision for her soul's journey.
And she commended her soul into the hands of God in the fifteenth year from her coming to Kartli, in the year 338 from the Ascension of Christ, and in the year 5838 from the beginning of the world.
Then these two cities, Mtskheta and Ujarma, and all Kartli were shaken by her death.
And they came and buried her victory-clad body in that same place, at Bud, a village of Kkhoeti (!). And King Mirian and all the people departed, for they were building the upper church with stone.
And they finished it in the fourth year. And King Mirian died and was buried at the middle southern pillar, on the north side.
And inside that pillar is a piece of the Living Pillar.
And in the second year his wife Nana died and was buried on the west side of the same pillar where King Mirian had been buried.
And Bakur, son of Rev, became king. And Bishop John died, and James, the priest who had come from that same place, became archbishop.
And in the twenty-third year after the raising of the Precious Cross, a burial canopy was made for Rev, and a tomb was built in the lower church.
And Rev died and was buried with his wife. And after him, in the tenth year, this Bakur began the church of Tsilkani and finished it in the thirty-fifth year.
And he died and was buried in the Lower Church. And his brother Trdat became king.
And the archbishop was Job, deacon of Nerses, catholicos of the Armenians. And the king brought out a canal for [?] a canal [?] and laid the foundation of a church.
And in his time also a church was built to completion at Nekresi in Kakheti. And after him Varaz-Bakur was installed as king.
And in his time the marzpans of the king of the Persians came into Siunia, and he withdrew to Khidar [?]. And the archbishop was that same Job.
And then Kram Khuar-Borzard, pitiakhsh of the Persian king, came to the city of Tbilisi, to the fortress.
And Kartli came under his tribute, as did Armenia, Siunik and Vaspurakan.
And in his time the nobles built the holy church at Mtskheta and endowed [?] the great church with villages and kardags [?] [?]
in Kartli. And after him Bakur, son of Trdat, reigned. And the archbishop was Elijah.
And he built a church at Bolnisi. And he went out from there and restored the Armazis for fear of the Persians.
And after him Parsman, the sister's son of Trdat, reigned. And the archbishop was Simeon. And after him Mirdat reigned.
And the pitiakhsh Varash took him away to Baghdad, and he died there. And after him Archil reigned, and the archbishop was Jonah.
And at that time the Lower Church collapsed. And Jonah moved to the church of Gareubani and brought the Living Pillar with him.
And in his time the nobles built Holy Stephen on the Aragvi. And the magi at Mogveta practiced their magian rites in the service of fire.
And in the time of this same Archil four archbishops passed away. And then Mirdat reigned.
And the archbishop was Glonokor. And this archbishop was also made eristavi of Kartli and Hereti by the pitiakhsh Barazbod.
And after him the great Vakhtang Gorgasali reigned, and the archbishop was Joel. At that time the Persians took Vakhtang away.
And after some time he returned, and the archbishop was Michael. And he struck King Vakhtang in the mouth with his foot.
And the king sent envoys to Greece and asked the emperor and the patriarch for a catholicos.
And he gave Peter as catholicos. And with him was Samuel the monk, holy and worthy.
And King Vakhtang built the Lower Church and installed Peter as catholicos. And this was in the 170th year from the conversion of Kartli.
Ten kings had passed away, and thirteen archbishops. And the first catholicos was Peter.
And after this Dachi of Ujarma reigned, and the catholicos was Samuel. And in his time people settled at Tbilisi, and they built the holy church of (Mary).
And the catholicos was Peter. And after this Bakur, son of Dachi, reigned, and the catholicos was Samuel.
And after him reigned Parsman, and the catholicos was Tavpachag.
And in his time also Chimaga [?] 6 [?]. And in his time also the kingdom of the Persians came to Mtskheta and threw Kartli and its cities into turmoil, and departed.
And after him reigned another Parsman, and the catholicos was Dasabia, a native of Mtskheta.
And from this point two houses of native Mtskhetans took up the catholicosate. And in the time of that same king the catholicos was Evlale.
At that time the blessed John of Zedazeni came from Mesopotamia of Assyria; he and his twelve disciples came with him.
And after him Bakur reigned, and the catholicos was Macarius. And in his time also Varsken was pitiakhsh. And Shushanik was martyred at Tsurtavi.
And after him the catholicos was Samuel, and then Simon-Peter. And in the time of that same Bakur the kingship of Kartli came to an end.
At that time Mtskheta was dwindling and Tbilisi was being built up; Armazi was declining and Kala was growing great.
The Persians ruled over Kartli, Armenia, Siunik and Vaspurakan; and the catholicos was Samuel, and slowly Kartli was gathered together again.
And they appointed Guaram as eristavi, and later also as curopalates. He laid the foundation of the Holy Cross, and in his time the catholicos was another Samuel.
And the inhabitants of Tbilisi began the great church: all the people built one half and the eristavis the other half; and the catholicos was Bartholomew.
And after him his son Stephen, brother of Demetrius, was eristavi, and he built the church of the Cross.
At that time Heraclius, king of the Greeks, came through. And the commander of the fortress called out from Kala of Tbilisi to King Heraclius, taunting him as a he-goat [?].
And he stretched out his feet [?], took up Daniel and searched out this (saying):
"The he-goat of the west will come and will shatter the horns of the ram of the east."
And the king said to him: "If the matter (concerning me) turns out so, I will repay you your reward."
And he left Jibgho the eristavi behind to fight. And he himself went to Baghdad to fight King Khosrow.
And a few days later this Jibgho took the citadel. He seized the commander of the fortress and filled his mouth with drachmas.
And then he flayed him alive and sent the skin after the king to Gardabani, into the land of Varaz-Grigol.
Heraclius went and destroyed Baghdad. He seized King Khosrow and made him hand over the Wood of Life.
And by his order he began to rebuild Jerusalem, and he installed Modestus as patriarch. And he came back this way in the seventh year.
And before he came to Tbilisi, Sioni had been separated [?] by the inhabitants, but the church of the Cross was still lacking.
This Heraclius sent heralds to Tbilisi, Mtskheta and Ujarma,
so that all the Christians in the cities would gather in the churches, and all the magi and fire-worshippers would either be baptized or be shot down.
But they did not want baptism, and they slyly mingled with the Christians, until he turned the sword on all of them, and rivers of blood flowed in the churches.
And Heraclius purified the law of Christ and departed. And the same great Stephen was eristavi, and the catholicos was Bartholomew, for the second time [?].
And after that Adarnase was eristavi, and in his time three catholicoi succeeded one another: John, Babila and Tabor.
And after him his son Stephen was eristavi. He separated [?] the church of the Cross and established an assembly at the Cross on the feast of the Cross, for one month.
And Stephen took his seat in Tbilisi, and the catholicos was Samuel. And after him [?] — Evnon.
And news came that the Hagarenes had captured Baghdad. Because of this the Greeks loaded earth of the land onto a mule and carried it off to Greece.
And after him Guaram the curopalates ruled as eristavi, 6th; and Guaram the Child, 7th; and then Arshusha the curopalates, 8th; and Varaz-Bakur Apa the patrician,
who converted the people of Garbani, 9th; and then Nerse [10th]; and his sons: Philip, 11th; Stephen, 12th; Adarnase, 13th; Guaram, 14th; and Bakurian, son of Baldad (!)
15th; and the sons of Adarnase: Stephen, 16th; and Ashot the curopalates, 17th; and Guaram [18th]. These were the great eristavis.
And the catholicoi who came from Evnon onward: Tavpachag, 1st; Evlale, 2nd; Joel, 3rd; Samuel, 4th; George, 5th; Cyrion, 6th; Izidbozid, 7th; Theodore, 8th; Peter, 9th. These.
These nine were married men. Then: Mama, 1st; John, 2nd; Gregory, 3rd; Clement, 4th; Sarmean, 5th; Talele, 6th; Samuel, 7th; Cyril, 8th;
Gregory, 9th; Samuel, 10th; George, 11th; Gabriel, 12th; Hilarion, 13th; Arsenius, 14th; Evsukh [?], 15th; Basil, 16th; Michael, 17th; David, 18th; Arsenius, 19th.
Chapter 2. Now when the holy and blessed queen Nino had completed her course in the faith of the Holy Trinity,
she who became for us the evangelist of our hearts and the healer of our souls and bodies, and set apart this one kingdom, the land of the north,

the kingdom of the kings of Mtskheta, she made everyone believe in the confession of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit; through baptism, in the coming of Christ and his birth from the holy Virgin,
the baptism and death of Christ and his resurrection from the dead, immortality and life after death, and the second coming of the Son of God to earth,
…the life of the righteous and the punishment of sinners, for His is the kingdom forever and ever, and beyond. Amen.
as she reached the land of Kukheti, at the village of Bodi, she fell ill with the sickness from which she also died.
Then the kings of the land gathered, and the princes with their wives, and a great crowd of powerful people, for everyone looked upon Nino's face
as if it were the face of an angel from heaven. They wore her small, old garment to shreds, kissing it with faith and insistence [?].
All the queens sitting around her begged her, with streams of tears running down from their eyes because they were losing their teacher, the ascetic, the skilled healer of the sick.
Queen Salome of Ujarma and Perozhavri of Siunia spoke to her, and all the princes with them asked her, saying:
"Where did you come from, and how did you come to our land to be our savior? Where were you brought up, lady?
Tell us your story! Why do you speak of captivity, you who set captives free, blessed one?
For we have learned from you that there were prophets before the Son of God came to earth, and after them the twelve apostles,
And again, the seventy-two; and God has sent no one to us except you.
And how can you say, 'I am a captive,' or 'as in India' [?]? Then Nino began to speak and said:
"Daughters of the faith, those near to God, my queens, I see you as being like those first holy women in all faith and love of God.
You want to know the ways of your poor handmaid, and I will tell you.
See, my soul has come up to my throat; I am about to fall asleep forever with the sleep of my mother.
So bring writing materials and write down my poverty and my unworthy life,
so that your children too may know of your faith and of how you received me, and of God's miracles,
some of which you have seen: on the mountains, in the bramble thicket, at the raising of the pillar, and there by the spring, up until I came here.
The Lord himself knows, and my soul knows, what my eyes have seen come down from heaven onto the earth."
Then Salome of Ujarma and Perozhavri of Siunia took up writing materials.
And holy Nino began to speak, and they wrote. She began with the affairs of her parents, before her birth.
Chapter 3. The Life of Saint Nino. It was in those times when George of Cappadocia was martyred for Christ,
in those days a certain man from the city of Cappadocia, worthy of the rank of princes, a servant of God, went to Rome, before the kings, to serve and to receive a reward.
And in those same days there was a certain man in Colastra, and he had two children: a son and a daughter.
His son's name was Juvenal, and his daughter's Susanna. And when those parents died, their children were left orphans.
They got up and went to the holy city of Jerusalem. They put their hope in the hope of all Christians, the Holy Resurrection, and gave themselves into its care there.
This brother of Susanna attained the office of [?] (devtalaroba), and Susanna served Miapor, Sarah of Bethlehem.
This Cappadocian youth came before the king in Rome. The Brangs had drawn up in battle array against the Romans on the plain of Pitalani.
God gave that Cappadocian youth invincible strength, and he stood mightily against the enemy until he put them to flight.
He captured the king of the Brangs and many princes with him, and he brought the king of the Brangs and all the princes before the king.
The king ordered that they be put to death. Then the Brangs began to weep, and they begged Zabilon:
"First give us your law and bring us into the temple of your God, and then let us die,
for it was you who captured us, so you should do this for us, and you will be innocent of our blood."
As soon as Zabilon heard this, he quickly reported their words to the king and the patriarch.
They were baptized under Zabilon's hand, and they were brought into the temple of God, the holy church, and given communion in the mysteries of Christ.
They were shown the glories of the holy apostles.
Early in the morning the Brangs rose, put on their burial garments, and went out to the place where men were executed.
They prayed and thanked God for their baptism and communion, saying:
"In death we are immortal, for God has made us worthy to see such glory and to receive the inexhaustible provision for the journey, the body and blood of Christ,
the Son of God, the immortal King, who is higher than all heights and deeper than all depths, for he is blessed forever and ever. Amen.
But woe to our offspring, fruits of bitterness, heirs of darkness." And they cried out: "Let the swordsman come and take our heads from us."
When Zabilon saw this, he was deeply moved and wept, for they had stretched out their own heads to be slaughtered like sheep, and they grieved for their children as for lambs.
Then Zabilon went before the king and begged for their release, and the king let them go with gifts.
They begged Zabilon to go with them to their land and give the law of Christ and baptism with water to all their people.
Zabilon agreed to their request. He asked the patriarch for priests and received the king's order, and they set out with joy.
When they were about one day's journey away, news arrived that the king was returning alive, with all the princes with him.
Then those ten eristavates set out: Kholama and Khozaba, Khlacha, Kheneshagi, Timgaragi, Zaka, Gza, Zarga, Zarda,
Zarma, and the royal Tmonigoni [?], and they came to meet him at the great river Ghdamara. And the king divided those people and stationed them on this side and that side of the water.
The priests blessed the river, and all the people went down into the river and were washed, and they came up by a single exit.
For ten days Zabilon laid his hands on all the people. They set up tents, the priests celebrated the service, and they gave the people communion in the mysteries of Christ.
And he dismissed the priests and set in order every rule of Christianity. And he left a blessing and went to Rome with great gifts.
And he considered in his heart and said: "Let me go to Jerusalem." And he gave all his possessions to the poor.
And that devtalari [?] had become patriarch. And Zabilon and the patriarch became great friends with each other.
Sara Miaphor said to the patriarch: "This Zabilon is the father and baptizer of the Brangs, a man perfect in wisdom and in the fear of God.
Give him your sister Susanna as his wife." And his words pleased the holy patriarch, and they gave Susanna to him as his wife.
And they went to their own city, Colastri. And I alone was born of them. And they are my parents.
And my mother raised me in her bosom, in the service of the poor, day and night without ceasing.
And when I was twelve years old, my parents sold everything they had and went to Jerusalem.
Then my father received the sign of the cross from the patriarch and parted from my mother.
And she pressed me to her breast and poured her tears from her eyes over my face like streams. And she said to me:

"You, my only daughter, behold, I leave you an orphan without me, and I entrust you to the God of heaven, the Father, the Nourisher and Lord of all, for he is the father of orphans and the judge of widows.
Do not be afraid, my child! But take up the zeal of Mary Magdalene, and of the sisters of Lazarus, for the love of Christ.
And if you fear him as they did, he will likewise give you everything you ask of him, whenever you want anything from him."
And he gave me a kiss for eternity and went away beyond the Jordan with those men of the wilderness; what became of him, his Lord Jesus knows.
And the patriarch gave my mother as a servant to the poor, to infirm women. And I served Miaphor, the Armenian from Dvin, for two years.
And I asked her about the passion of Christ, about his crucifixion, burial and resurrection, and about his garment, the crosses, the linen cloths and the shroud, everything in order,
for there had never been, nor was there in Jerusalem, anyone equal to her in knowledge of the law, in all the way of both the Old and the New.
She began to teach me and said: "I see your strength, my child, like the strength of a lioness, which roars over all four-footed beasts,
or like a female eagle, which rises higher into the heights of the air than the male, and the whole earth, in the pupil of her eye,
is small like a pearl; she holds still and surveys it, makes out her prey, sees it like a flash of fire, lets her wings rustle, and swoops down upon it.
So may your life be, under the guidance of the Holy Spirit."
Chapter 4. The written account of the same Salome of Ujarma. Now I will begin and tell you everything: when mortal men saw the immortal God on earth, who had come from him, Israel turned back.
And there came the calling of all the foreign nations, who served foreign gods, for he himself willed the salvation of the world which he had created.
He began to do good to the Jews: raising the dead, giving sight to the blind, and healing all the sick.
They grew envious [?] of this, took counsel together, and sent soldiers throughout the whole land, to come in haste.
And they said: "Behold, we are perishing!" Then Jewish men came from every region, learned in the law of Moses,
They rose up against the Holy Spirit, and they carried out what Christ willed of them: they crucified him and cast lots for his garment.
By lot the tunic of the Lord Jesus fell to the northerners, the people of Mtskheta. And they buried their Creator and sealed the tomb.
But he rose, as he had said before. When it dawned, the linen cloths were lying in the tomb.
Pilate looked into all this and came to the tomb with his wife. They found the linen cloths, and Pilate's wife took them.
She had become a believer in Christ, and she went in great haste to Pontus, to her own home.
After a long time the cloths came into the hands of Luke the Evangelist, and he put them where he alone knows.
But the shroud was not found, just as the body of Christ was not found.
Some said that Peter was able to take it and kept it, but that he did not tell of it openly as he told everything else.
The crosses are buried in this city, but no one knows where. When God wills, they will be revealed.
Then I gave blessing to the Lord God, and thanks to my lady for all this account.
And I asked again, "Where is that northern land, and where is the garment of our Lord?"
She said to me, "The northern land is the mountain country of Armenia. It is a pagan land under the rule of the Greeks and the Ujiks."
In those days a woman from Ephesus came to worship at the Holy Resurrection, and Niaphore asked that woman:
"Is Queen Helena also in the same darkness, and is their kingdom without God?" And she said to him:
"I am their servant and close to all their counsels, and the Romans have a great desire for Christ, for the faith and for baptism."
And I said to Miaphor: "Send me, and let me go before Queen Helena; perhaps she will let me come near to give an answer before her concerning Christ."
And she told the patriarch. And he summoned me, my holy father the patriarch, my mother's brother,
and he stood me on the step of the altar and laid his hands on my shoulders. And he sighed toward heaven and said:
"Lord God of the fathers and of the ages, into your hands I commend this orphan, my sister's child, and I send her out to preach your divinity and to proclaim the good news of your resurrection;
wherever her course is pleasing to you, Christ, be to her a way, a fellow-traveller, a harbour, a teacher, a tongue of knowledge, as you were to those of old who feared your name."
And he separated me from my mother and gave me the cross and a blessing as provisions for the road. And I set out with that woman.
When we came to her house, we found there a lady of royal kin named Rhipsime. She was waiting for baptism from Jerusalem and longed to confess Christ.
Then that woman entrusted me into her hands, and I baptized her under my hand, together with forty souls of her household.
And we went to her house and stayed there two years. Then the Lord looked upon the land of the Greeks, and the tenth, Constantine, came to believe,
and he and his mother and all their court confessed Christ, in the year 5444 from the beginning of the world, and 311 from the Ascension of Christ.
And all Greece was turned toward Christianity. In the seventh year the holy council took place at Nicaea, and in the eighth year was our flight from Greece.
The lady Rhipsime, and Gaiane her nurse, and fifty souls set out on the fifteenth of the first month, and we came into the lands of Armenia, to the garden of King Trdat.
They were killed there on the thirtieth of the first month, on a Friday. But I remained among the thorns of the rose bushes, for the rose and the almond were in bloom at that time.
And as the souls of those saints were rising up, I saw a deacon coming down from heaven, in the likeness of a garment, with a stole of light.
And in his hands he held a censer, from which came forth fragrant smoke that covered the heavens.
And with him was a multitude of the hosts of heaven. And those holy souls joined those heavenly hosts and rose up with glory into heaven.
But I cried out: "Lord, Lord, why have you left me among asps and vipers?" I heard a voice from there, which said to me:
"Thus shall your taking away be: when those thorns that surround you have all become purple roses, made fragrant through you."
But you, arise and go to the east, where the harvest is great and there are no labourers at all."
So I set out and came to Ulopor[eti] [?], and I spent the winter there in great hardship.
In the fourth month I went into the mountains of Javakheti, to find out where Mtskheta was. And on a mountain I came upon
