And I took to a hard and harsh road, and I saw great hardships from the roads and terrors from wild beasts, until I arrived here, where the water began to flow toward the east.
From then on I had relief. And I found travelers and reached the territories of Kartli,
the city of Urbnisi, and I saw a foreign people, servants of foreign gods: they worshipped fire and stones and wood.
My soul grieved over their perdition. I went to the synagogue of the Jews because of the Hebrew language, and I stayed there for one month and studied the condition of this land.
One day great crowds, countless in number, set out from that city and went to the great city of Mtskheta,
which was the seat of the great kings, to trade and to pray to Armaz, their god.
I went along with them, and we reached the city of Mtskheta, on the far side, at Mogvta. We stopped there on the bridge and watched that fire-worshipping people.
I wept over their magian religion and their error, because of their perdition, and I also mourned my own exile.
Chapter 6. The arrival of Saint Nino in Mtskheta, recorded by the same Salome of Ujarma. On the next day there was the sound of horn [?] and of trumpet.
And a countless people came out; like ones adorned with flowers, awesome and terrifying, they came out. But the king had not yet set out.
When the hour came, everyone fled and hid here and there, and everyone took refuge under cover, because Queen Nana was coming out.
After Queen Nana had passed, only then did all the people slowly come out.
They decorated all the streets with garments of every kind and with leaves. And all the people began to praise the king.
And then King Mirian came out with an indescribable [?] vision. And I asked the Jewish woman:
"What is this?" And she said to me: "The God of gods [?] that Armaz of theirs, which is nothing other than an idol [?]."
So I went to see Armaz. The mountains were filled with banners and people, as if with flowers.
I hurried ahead to the fortress of Armazi and stood near that idol, in a crack in the wall. I watched wonders and dreadful things
It cannot be told by the tongue how soul-shaking the dread was, with fear and trembling, for those kings and for all the people.
I saw a terrifying figure standing there. Behold, there stood a man of bronze. On his body he wore a coat of golden mail and a golden helmet. On his shoulders were set [?] ("prtskhili") and beryl.
In his hand he held a sharpened sword, which gleamed and turned in his hand, as though whoever touched it would hand himself over to death. And they were saying:
"Woe if I fall short in any way in the glory of the great god Armazi, or err in any word with the Hebrews, or have merely fallen into listening to the magi, the servants of the sun.
And some ignorant people speak of a certain great God of the heavens; may he not find some blemish in me and strike me with that sword of his, of which all the earth is afraid."
And all worshipped in fear. And on his right stood an idol of gold, and its name was Gatsi.
On his left stood a silver idol, and its name was Ga. Your fathers from Arian-Kartli had held these as gods.
Then I wept and sighed to God over the errors of those northern lands: the light was hidden and darkness held sway.
I saw those mighty kings and all the princes, and how they had been swallowed alive by the devil, as the dead are swallowed by hell.
They called stones and wood their creator. They worshipped as god bronze, iron and brass hammered out over the bellows.
These they held to be the creators of heaven and earth. Then I remembered the word that the patriarch Juvenal, my holy father, had commanded me, namely:
"I am sending you out as a mature man, and you are to reach a foreign land, the peoples Dgeveli, Zepheli and Narkadoveli, who are men hateful to God, warlike and hostile."
Then I lifted my eyes to heaven and said: "Lord, Lord, through the greatness of your power these enemies of yours will cringe before you.
It is because of your great long-suffering that these enemies, the ashes of the earth, do whatever they devise.
But do not disregard them, for man is your image. For his sake one of the Trinity became man and saved the whole world.
"Look upon these peoples too, and be angry with these invisible spirits, the rulers of the world, the princes of this darkness.
And show me, O God of my father and my mother, me, this handmaid of yours, the child of your servant,
so that all the ends of the earth may see your salvation, and the north may rejoice together with the south, and every tongue may worship you, the only God, through Jesus Christ our Lord,
to whom it is fitting to offer thanksgiving and glory, now and always and in the ages to come. Amen."
And in the twinkling of an eye, the air and the winds stirred from the west, and thunder sounded with a terrifying voice.
And a swift cloud appeared, fearful to look at. And the breeze from the west brought a [?] breath of bitterness and stench.
Then everyone fled to the countryside and to the city. And they had time to get into their homes.
And all at once that cloud of wrath arrived and brought hail, each stone as heavy as a litra, on that place alone. It smashed the idols, ground them down and crushed them to powder.
And the fierce wind demolished those walls and hurled them down onto the rock, which you too have seen, or perhaps not. And the king said with tears:
"Hē, hē, raith-meboy khojat stabanub rasul psarzad." And the translation is this: "You speak the truth, blessed queen and apostle of the Son of God."
And when the wrath had died down, I came out of the cleft in the rock and found that beryl stone.
I picked it up and went on toward the far end of the rock, where the old city had been. A fortress had stood in that place.
And a beautiful [?] tree stood there, tall and with many branches. I came under that tree and marked on myself the sign of the cross of Christ. And I prayed there for six days.
When you, the crowd of the people, came out and looked for those gods that had been destroyed, and did not find them, I was there then,
for it was the sixth day of that month, the day on which Emmanuel on Tabor showed the image of the Father to the chief ones of the living and the chief ones of the dead.
Then this sister of mine, Sroshana, a lady of the royal court, came. She saw me, brought a Greek-speaking woman, and asked me about my whole journey.
Then I saw tears flowing from her eyes because I was a stranger.
When she had learned everything about me, she pressed me to let her take me to the palace, but I did not want to go, and she left.
And on the third day I came down to the city of Mtskheta and made my way to the king's garden.
When I reached the gate of the garden, there was a small hut belonging to the gardener. When I went in, this woman Anastasia was sitting there.

And when he saw me, he rose and embraced me warmly, as an acquaintance and friend, and he washed my feet and anointed me with oil, and he set a table before me with wine and urged me to eat and drink.
And I stayed with him for nine months. She was childless, and she and her husband were anxious about it. In a vision I saw a man the color of light come, and he said to me:
"Go into the garden. Under the [?] fir trees there is a small place, lovingly prepared. Take earth from that place and give it to these people to eat, and they will have children."
And I did so. And they had many sons and daughters, as you yourselves see.
And in those same days, two and three times, I saw a vision during my light slumber, resting upon my knees:
the birds of heaven would come and go down into the river. They would bathe, then come to that garden and pluck at the [?], and feed on the flowers.
And they cried out to me pitifully, as if that paradise were mine; they came up to me from outside with twittering and called out to me. Their appearance was many-colored and beautiful.
And this happened many times. And I told this to my sister, the daughter of Abiathar. She answered and said to me:
"Stranger and native-born, captive and deliverer of captives, know that the new time has come upon you, and through you that old report will be heard,
the deed of our fathers, the unjust shedding of the innocent blood of that heavenly man, by which God brought shame upon the Jews:

their scattering to the ends of heaven, the fall of the kingdom, the taking away of that holy temple, the winning of that foreign people, the calling of them his own, and the giving of glory to them."
And again she said: "Jerusalem, Jerusalem, how your children have been stripped from you [?]! And you will gather the peoples from all the ends of heaven under your wings."
"Behold, this woman has come here too, and she will change the whole order of this land." And she turned to me and said:
"This is the meaning of your vision: through you this place of the garden will become a paradise for the glorifying of God, to whom be glory now and always and to the ages of ages, amen."
Chapter 7, which a Jewish woman wrote, named Sidonia, the daughter of Abiathar the priest. And it was when God looked with mercy upon this forgotten land of the north, of the Caucasians,
the highlands of Armenia, whose mountains were covered with fog, and its plains with the mist of error and ignorance,
and this land was in shadow, cut off from the Sun of Righteousness, from the coming and the knowledge of the Son of God, just as it was rightly called by the name "North" (chrdilo, "shadow").

This is not to say that it lacked the light of this sun, or lacks it now. Everyone under heaven sees the sun, and it sees everything. Even the places it holds back its heat from, it looks upon with its light.
That is not why this land was called "the North" (Shadow). Rather, so many years and so many generations had passed since Noah, Eber and Abraham.
And in that time lived Job the nobleman, tested by the Tempter, as were Joseph, Moses, Joshua, the priests and the judges, one after another, whom we know from hearing the divine books.
There passed until the coming of Christ 5,500 years; from the birth of Christ until the crucifixion, 33; and from the crucifixion of Christ until the baptism of Constantine, king of the Greeks, 311;
And fourteen years after that, Nino, the preacher of truth and our queen, was sent to our land,
just as, in the darkness, the morning star rises and the dawn breaks, and after it rises that great ruler of the day.
Such was our life, O Georgians: we went about in the light, yet we dwelt in darkness. We rejoiced in pleasure while we stored up mourning, and there was no one to comfort us in it.
We served created things and not the Creator. Instead of Him who sits upon the chariots of the cherubim, our fathers worshipped high mountains: Ebal
and Gerizim. And on it there was neither God, nor Moses, nor any sign of them, but only lifeless idols of stone.
In this land of Kartli there were two mountains, and on them two idols, Armaz and Zaden, which with foul breath took in the smell of a thousand souls of firstborn children.
Armaz and Zaden. Their parents gave the children to them as an offering and sacrifice, as though there would never be death again [?]. And this went on until now.
There were also other royal idols, Gatsi and Ga. To them one royal child was sacrificed: it was burned in fire, and the ashes were scattered over the head of the idol.
After all this, I will tell you my father's account, which I know from reading books and from what my father told me.
When Herod was reigning, we heard here that the Persians had seized Jerusalem.
a letter of mourning had been written to all the Jews of Kartli, to the inhabitants of Mtskheta, the priests of Bodi, the scribes of Kodistsqaro, and the interpreters of Sobiskanani [?], saying:
"Twelve kings have come to conquer our land."
Everyone hurried to set out to help them. But a little later another message, this one of comfort, came from Jerusalem to the whole land, saying:
"Those Persians did not come to conquer the land. Instead of armour, weapons and provisions, they had yellow gold,
myrrh, which quickly heals wounds, and fragrant incense. Each of their horsemen had these.
Each of the kings themselves had one load of these, and they were looking for a certain newborn child, a son of David. They found him, a stranger,
the son of a stranger woman, born at the wrong time in a place that was no proper place, as is usual for those who live as outsiders.
They came to that child and worshipped him, and they offered him all these gifts. Then they crossed the mountain and left in peace.
Now do not be afraid, Jews. I, Herod, searched and did not find that child or his mother.
But now I will turn the sword on every infant two years old and under, and he will perish along with them. So now be at ease,
for all this was an illusion." Thirty years after this, the priest Annas wrote from Jerusalem to my grandfather Oziah, saying:
"That same child, to whom the kings of the Persians had come with gifts, has grown up and reached the full measure of adulthood.

to that water of the Jordan, to the son of Zechariah, all the tribes of Israel were going out, and your father's mother's brother Elioz was with them too. And behold, the heaven thundered and the earth shook,
the mountains trembled, the hills danced, the sea stood still, the waters flowed upward, the son of Zechariah fled, and terror and trembling fell on all of us.
Because of the great crowd of people, we kept silent about this matter, which had indeed been known to God from eternity."
In the fourth year, a command came out from Jerusalem from King Herod, saying:
"To all the sons of Israel scattered across every land: see one God, take heed, and listen to one law.
Learn the one word of Moses, which he spoke: 'Whoever on earth calls himself God, let him be hanged on a tree.'
and then he said: "Cursed be everyone who is hung on a tree." Now behold, a certain man has arisen, and his name is Jesus,
who of his own accord calls God his Father, as though he himself were God. Come, all of you, to his death, and let us fulfill the commandment of God and of Moses."
And from here went my father's mother's brother Elioz, an old man. His mother was of the tribe of Eli the priest, and Elioz had only one sister.
His mother pleaded with her son and said to him: "Go, my child, at the king's summons and according to the rule of the law.
But whatever they plot, do not let your mind join in it at all. No, my child,
for this is the word of the prophets and the parable of the wise. It is a mystery hidden from the Jews, but for the gentiles it is light and eternal life."
And Elioz and all the Jews went from Kartli. And everything that we now know through Nino, from the Gospels, through Christ, was fulfilled.
And the garment fell by lot to this land, and Elioz brought it.

But as for his mother, when the sound was heard, when the guard struck the smith's hammer on the three nails on the cross in Jerusalem, she heard the sound here, and that woman cried out bitterly and said:
"Farewell, kingdom of the Jews, for you have killed your own Savior and Redeemer, and from now on you have become enemies of the Creator.
Woe is me, that I did not die before, so that I would not have heard this, and that I did not stay alive a little longer,
"Would that I had seen the light shining forth upon the Gentiles and the glory of the people of Israel." And at this word that woman, the mother of Elioz, passed to her rest.
And this Elioz brought that tunic of the Savior Jesus Christ to Mtskheta, to our house, and he saw that his mother had died at those words.
And his sister came out to meet him, drenched in tears as if in blood. She threw her arms around her brother's neck, took that garment of Jesus from him, and pressed it to her breast.
And at once her spirit departed because of these three bitter things: her mother's death, and even more her pain at the death of Christ, and her longing for that garment.
Then there was a great commotion in Mtskheta among the kings, the princes and all the people.
And King Amazaer saw that garment of Jesus and wanted to take it away. But he was seized by dread at the dead woman's grip on it, and he was afraid and did not dare.
And Elioz buried his sister, and she held that garment in her hands.
And that place exists. God knows it, and my mother Nino knows it, but she does not tell, for it is not right to speak of it now.
But let this alone be enough for Nino's disciples and for the believers in Christ: the place is near that cedar which came from Lebanon and was planted in Mtskheta.
Besides this, I heard from my father: "There is also another thing clothed with power, the double one too, the mantle of Elijah, in this city, in our hands,
beneath the firm foundation of the altar, incorrupt among the stones until its time." For my mother Nino many times sent me to my father,
so that I might sincerely search out the place of that garment. And he thus laid a portion [?] with me and said to me:
"Here is its burial place, where the tongues of men have not fallen silent in singing to God; upon it is that place,
like the place of Jacob, seen as a ladder and reaching up to heaven, from now and forever, with glory and praise unceasing."
Chapter 8, told by the same woman, Sidonia. When I, Sidonia, the daughter of Abiathar, saw Saint Nino at the top of the fortress of former Mtskheta, on that high tower, beneath those bronzes [?],
[?] sat in the king's cool places and resting places, at the time when the Lord shattered Armaz and the other idols with the terrifying wrath of his face,
as is written earlier in her testament, until Queen Nana came to believe in Christ God as the Son of God.
the blessed Saint Nino spent six years, as she herself tells of her stay there, and when at length she made seven of us women disciples in his law,
for she performed many healings in secret, until by God's providence she began to heal openly.
God first showed his power through her on Queen Nana, in the bramble thicket,
and through her prayer he healed the queen of a severe illness that human skill had been unable to heal.
After that the chief of the magi, the Persian prince Khuara, fell ill. He was cruelly tormented by an evil spirit and had come near to death.
This prince was the brother of Queen Nana's mother. Then Queen Nana pleaded with my mother Nino;
and the king too was observing the matter little by little, and he said to Nino doubtfully: "By the power of which god do you do this work of healing?
Are you a daughter of Armaz, or a child of Zaden? You came here as a stranger and fell down before them, and now mercy [?] is upon you,
and they have granted you the power of healing, so that you may make your living by it in this foreign land. May they be glorified forever!
So stay before me always, like one of the nurses, honoured in this land. But do not speak that foreign word, the faith of those misguided Romans,
and do not wish to speak of it here at all. For behold, here are the gods who give great harvests and rule the world, who spread the sunlight and give the rain,
who make the fruits of the earth grow, the gods of Kartli, Armaz and Zaden, who search out everything hidden,
and the ancient gods of our fathers, Gatsi and Ga. And let you yourself serve to make people believe in them.
And now, if you heal this prince, I will make you rich and settle you in Mtskheta as a servant of Armaz. Although he was shattered by the violence of that storm, his place remains unshaken.
This Armaz and Itrushana, the god of the Chaldeans, are bitter enemies.
The one brings the sea against the other, and the other cannot bring anything at all against the first [?], as is the custom of the rulers of the world. Let this command of mine be enough for you."
The blessed Nino answered the king and said: "O king, may you live forever in the name of Christ, through the intercession of his holy Mother and of all the saints with her.
May God, the Creator of heaven and earth, the Maker of everything created, send upon you,
out of his great glory and his countless mercy, one spark of his grace, like a spark from a furnace,
so that you may know and understand the righteousness of heaven and the light of the sun, the depth of the sea and its foundations,
the breadth of the earth and its foundations, and so that it may be made known to you, O king, who clothed the heavens with clouds and the thunders with the voice of the air,
and the earth would shake at his fury, and thunderbolts would run, and in his track fire would blaze with his anger,
or when the great dragon that is in the sea stirs and shakes the whole earth, until the firm mountains and the rocks are broken;
and may he make you know all this thoroughly, for God is in the heavens, and he himself is invisible to all creation, except to him who came forth from him.
This One was sent to earth as a man. He accomplished everything for which He had come, and ascended to those same heights, to be with the Father.
He alone has seen the One who has no beginning, and He alone is with Him who looks upon the lowly and knows the lofty from afar.
But now, O king, the time when you will draw near to God is close. I see that there is a wonder in this city: the robe of the Son of God.
Some have said that the mantle of Elijah is here too, and there are many wonders here which God Himself has made known to them.
And I will heal this nobleman by the power of my Christ and by the cross of His passion,
just as God healed Queen Nana of her grievous illness. And what I have made known to him, he will do, so that he may enlighten his own soul and bring his people near to God."
Then they brought that nobleman. Saint Nino took him, and me, and Queen Nana into the garden, under the fir trees. She stood him there and made him raise his hands toward the east.
And she made him say three times: "I renounce you, devil, and I follow Christ, the Son of God."
And Saint Nino wept, sighing from her soul, and asked God for help for that man, and we did the same with her for a whole day.
And quickly that evil [?] (the text reads 'daughter', probably for 'spirit') went out, and he and all his household became disciples of Saint Nino,
and he glorified God, the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, to whom be glory forever and ever. Amen.

Chapter 9, told by the same woman. And it happened one day at the beginning of summer, on the twentieth of the month of July, on a Saturday, that the king arose and went out to hunt in the direction of Mukhnari,

He went around the country of Mukhnari and went up into the high forests of the mountains of Tkhoti, so that he might look out over the great fortresses of Aspa, Kaspi and Uplistsikhe, and he went up to the summit of that mountain.
And just at midday the sun grew dark above him, and it became pitch-black night. A very deep darkness covered those regions and places.

Because of that distress and calamity all his people were scattered from one another. The king was left alone, and he wandered over the mountains and through the high forests, frightened and trembling.
And he stopped in one place and gave up hope of staying alive.
But God, who does good, turned his mind from ignorance to understanding and from unknowing to knowledge. He came to his senses, reasoned in his heart and said:
"Look, I see that I have called on Armaz and Zaden with a loud voice, and I have found no relief.
So now let me call on the One whom Nino preaches, the Cross and the Crucified, through hope in whom she works many healings.
Might He not now have the power to save me from this distress? For I am in hell while still alive, and I do not know
Whether destruction has come upon the whole earth and light has turned into darkness, or whether this affliction is for me alone." At once he cried out and said:
"God of Nino, illumine this darkness for me and show me my dwelling, and I will confess your name, and I will set up the wood of your cross and worship it,
and I will build a house for you as your house and as a place of prayer for me, and I will be obedient to Nino and to the law of the Romans."
As soon as he had said and spoken these words, day broke and the sun quickly shone out.
Then the king got down from his horse and fell face down on the ground, sighing and weeping.
He rose, stretched out his hands toward the east and said: "You are God over all gods and Lord over all lords,
the God whom Nino preaches. Your name is to be praised by everything created under heaven and on earth.
You saved me from distress, and when I called on your name you quickly turned my darkness into light.
See, I have come to know that you want to save me and bring me close to you. Now I will set up the wood of your cross in this place,
so that your holy name may be glorified by it, and this event and these miracles may be remembered forever." He took careful note of that place, then set off and came away.
When his men saw the light, those who had been scattered and in distress for a long time gathered together again.
The king called out and said to all his people:
"All you people, give glory to the God of Nino, for he is the eternal God, and praise belongs to him alone forever. Amen."
And Queen Nana and all the city went out to meet the king, for they had first heard of his being lost and then of his return in peace.
They met him at Kindzara and Ghart. There was great joy because he had returned safely.
Blessed Nino, as was her custom, was standing at evening prayer in the bramble thicket, and we were with her, fifty people.
When the king came in, the whole city was stirred up. The king cried out in a loud voice and said:
"Where is that foreign woman, who is my mother, and where is her God, my savior?"
When he heard that she was here in the bramble thicket, praying, the king turned aside with his whole army. He came, leapt down from the saddle and said to Nino:
"Am I now worthy to call on the name of your God, my savior?"
The holy woman taught him and quickly instructed him to worship Christ, the Son of God, facing east.
Then all the people groaned and wept, because they saw the tears of the king and queen flowing for joy and because of the great wonder that had taken place.
The next day he sent envoys to Greece. Blessed Nino taught every person, day and night, the true way of the faith.
Chapter 10. Written by the same, on the building of the churches. And the king spoke to Nino about building a church,
when the king and all the people had eagerly set out toward Christianity, before the coming of the priests from Greece.
The believing king said to Saint Nino: "Where shall I build a house for God?" And the blessed one said to him:
"Wherever the mind of kings is firm." And the king said to her: "I love those bramble bushes of yours, and my mind desires it there, but not thus [?],
rather, I will not spare the royal garden, the height of its firs, the fruitfulness of its [?] and the fragrance of its flowers,
"But in it I will build a temple for my prayer, which shall stand forever." And at once they brought timber and began to build.
And they cut down that fir tree and prepared it as a pillar, and on its roots they laid the foundation of the church.
And there was the terrible vision of the pillar and of its foundation, which is written above.
And when the time came to raise the pillar mentioned earlier, the builders began to raise it, and they could not.
Then a countless multitude gathered, and the king with them. They began to prepare all kinds of devices and machines.
Not only were they unable to raise it, they could not even move it.
And all the wisdom and contrivance of men came to nothing, so that through the raising of that pillar God might be wondrously glorified and people might be more firmly established in the faith.
And since they could not raise it and the work failed, the king and all the people went away, disheartened with grief, and they were sorrowful over this.
But blessed Nino stayed in the same place, and twelve other women with her. And that blessed one lamented and shed tears over the pillar.
And at about midnight these two mountains, Armazi and Zaden, seemed to be toppling forward, as if they were collapsing, and they dammed the waters of both rivers.
And the Mtkvari burst out and was terribly sweeping the city away. And from there arose terrible and dreadful sounds of captivity and flight.
Likewise the Aragvi came down from above the fortress, and there were terrible roarings.
And the women were frightened and fled, and I too with them. But the blessed holy Nino cried out:
"Do not be afraid, my sisters. Those mountains stand where they are, those waters flow where they are, and all the people are asleep.
But the way the mountains seemed to collapse rightly shows us that the mountains of unbelief have collapsed in Kartli.
And the waters that were dammed up mean that the blood of children sacrificed to demons has been stopped.

And these cries of captivity belong to a multitude of demons, for they are mourning their own desolation, because they are being driven out of this place by the power of the Most High and by the Cross of Christ.
Turn and pray to God, children!" And at once those sounds ceased, and there was nothing.
And holy Nino stood and stretched out her hands toward heaven and lifted her eyes to God, and she prayed and entreated
that the enemy might not hinder this work of the faith, on which the king and all the people had zealously set out.
And before the cock had yet crowed, a mighty army struck terror at all three gates and broke down the gates of the city.
And the city was filled with the Persian army, and at once there arose shrieks enough to make one faint with terror, and cries, and slaughter of the people, so that it seemed blood was flowing.
And the whole place was filled, and a multitude of shouts and swords came upon us, and our flesh melted and our souls failed.
And I was weeping for my father and for my kinsfolk, and suddenly I heard them calling out loudly:
"Thus commands Khuara, king of the Persians, and Khuaran Khuara, king of kings: spare every Jew from the edge of the sword."
When I heard this, I came to my senses, and I began to waver in doubt, I and those ten who were with me.
And the swordsmen had drawn near and were surrounding us and killing. And a voice was heard loudly: "King Mirian has been seized!"
And that courageous striver looked around and said: "Have they done this again? I know that he is in great distress."
And she gave thanks to God, for this was a sign of their destruction, and of the salvation of Kartli and the glory of this place.
And she consoled us like a skilled teacher, Saint Nino, truly and indeed a teacher and apostle of Christ.
And she turned to the host that was advancing on us and said to it: "Where are the kings of the Persians, Khuara and Khuan Khuara? Did you set out from Sabastan yesterday?
You have come quickly. Great indeed is your army, you are beyond all measure, and you have mightily shattered this city and put it to the sword.
I command the winds and breezes: go to the dark northern mountains of Kedar. The One from whom you flee has come here."
And she moved her right hand and traced the sign of the cross with her hand. At once that whole multitude of people vanished, and a great stillness fell.
And we glorified God and called holy and blessed Nino blessed.
And as dawn was just beginning to break, my sisters fell asleep, but I stayed awake. And holy Nino stood with her hands raised.
And behold, a youth came and stood over us, wholly clothed in light, and wrapped in a cloak like fire.
And he spoke some three words to blessed Nino, and she fell on her face.
Then the youth put his hand to the pillar, took hold of its top, lifted it, and carried it up to the height of the heavens.
Amazed, I went up and said to the blessed lady: "What is this?" But she bowed my head down to the ground.
And I began to weep in that terror. After a short time the blessed one rose, raised me up as well, and we withdrew from that place.
The women were still at a distance. And behold, I saw the pillar coming down like fire and drawing near to its base.
And as it happened, it stood over that base, raised about twelve cubits above the ground, and slowly came down onto its own cut stump,
for its base was its own root, from which the living pillar had been cut.
And just at early dawn the king had risen, his heart weighed down with cares, and he looked toward the garden, toward his church that had been begun, for his mind was fixed there.
And he saw there a light, like lightning reaching up to heaven, in that garden. He began to run, coming swiftly, and the multitude of all the people with him.
And when they came and saw that wonder, that pillar, shining with light, was coming down to its place,
as though it stood upon its base, and it became fixed there, untouched by human hands. Blessed was that hour in which this took place!
The city of Mtskheta was filled with fear and joy, and rivers of tears streamed down the king, the princes, and all the people, as they sighed from their souls,
and they glorified God and called blessed Nino blessed. And many miracles took place on that day.
Chapter 11. Told by the same. The first miracle. A certain Jew came, blind from birth, and approached that living pillar, and at once he gained his sight and glorified God.
2. A certain royal child, eight years old, a pagan, lay sick; his mother brought him in faith,
laid him on a bed before the pillar of light, which was truly clothed in light, and she implored blessed Nino, saying:
"Look, my lady, on this son of mine, who has come near to death, for I know that the one you serve and preach to us is the God of gods."
Then the blessed Nino touched her hand to the life-giving pillar, laid it on the boy, and said to him:
"Do you believe in Jesus Christ, the Son of the living God, who came in the flesh for the salvation of the whole world?"
And the child said to her: "Yes, queen, I believe in Jesus Christ, the savior of created beings." Then Saint Nino said to him:
"Be healed from now on, and glorify him by whose power you were healed." And quickly the child rose up as if he had no pain.
And great fear fell on the king and on the whole multitude of the people. And sick people with every kind of illness kept coming and being healed,
until the king made a wooden covering around the pillar and hid it from sight. And so the people touched the covering and were healed at once, and they glorified God, the worker of wonders.
And the king began to build a church in the garden with zeal and great joy.
Then the apostles came from Greece, an archbishop, priests and deacons, and they began to baptize all the people, as is written above.
Chapter 12. What Abiathar told, who was formerly a priest in the synagogue of the Jews in Mtskheta and was baptized at the hand of Nino.
I, Abiathar, was the priest to whom the priesthood had fallen by lot that year, when this blessed woman Nino came to Mtskheta.
At that time letters had come to me from Rome, from Egypt and from Babylon, from the Jews, from the priests and the scribes, in which it was written as follows:
"God has broken up the kingdom of the Jews. See, the prophets have fallen silent, for everything that the Spirit had moved them to speak has been fulfilled,
and we have been scattered over all the earth, and the Romans have taken our land under their rule, for we have sinned in every way and have angered God the Creator.
Now look at the books of Moses, who wrote all this for us: 'Whoever on earth calls himself God shall be hanged on a tree.'
Or perhaps we erred in the death of that Nazarene Jesus. For you see that in former times,
whenever our fathers sinned against God and forgot him entirely, he would give them over to a mighty ruler and to captivity.
But whenever they turned back and cried out, he would quickly deliver them from their distress. And we know from the Scriptures that this happened seven times.
But ever since they laid hands on that son of a poor stranger woman and killed him, God has lifted his hand against us;
he has broken up the kingdom, removed us from the temple of God, and utterly rejected our nation.
And now it is three hundred years since he has listened to our prayer at all, or shown us any relief.
It seems to me that that man was from heaven." And much more of this kind was written.
When I heard this, I began to question that woman Nino about Christ: where he came from, and for what reason God became man.
Then the blessed woman opened her mouth like a gushing spring and like a fountain that never runs dry.

She began from the things of eternity. She recited my own books by heart and explained them to me more fully. She roused me as one roused from sleep, and enlightened me as one who had fainted. She made me pity my fathers, and convinced me of the change of the Law,

until through her words I came to believe in Christ, the Son of God, in his Passion and his glorious Resurrection, and in his Second Coming in terror, and that he truly is the expectation of the Gentiles.
At that time my daughter and I were made worthy of the sprinkling and cleansing of sins, the font, that holy water,
which the prophet David longed for and could not attain. And again I heard the voice of the singers of the New Law,
which that same David longed for and did not reach. And I was made worthy to partake of the true flesh and blood of the Lamb of God, offered for the sins of the world,

whose taste and sight are sweet [cf. Psalm 34:8, 'taste and see']. And after this may the Lord grant my departure from the flesh, for my eyes have seen many miracles worked through Nino in Mtskheta in my days.
Now the house of Eliozi was in the western part of the city, at the gate of Mogveti [?], on the Kura river.
And there was a small shrine, their place of fasting, on which holy Nino raised the cross of Christ.
And there the children of the nobles from the heart of the city were baptized one after another by the hand of Jacob the priest and Prosilas the archdeacon.
And that place was called the Baptistery of the Nobles. And that place was greatly honored in our days, for it stood in the open field, with no buildings around it.
And in those days the Jews of Mtskheta grew very jealous of me, and they cut down the kilamo [?] tree that stood at the door of the shrine and adorned that place,
for its branches spread over the whole portico of the shrine. And they began to leave for wherever they had come from, all except the Barabeans,
of whose house fifty souls were baptized. And they settled in Mtskheta.
And King Mirian granted them a village called Tsikhe-Didi, and they were held in great honor by the king and the Christians, through the grace and teaching of blessed Nino.
And in those days letters arrived from Rome, from the holy patriarch, to blessed Nino, to King Mirian, and to all the Georgian people.
And an archdeacon of the Braj [?] was sent to offer praise and give a blessing, to receive the prayers of holy and blessed Nino, and to share in her grace.
And he carried a letter from the king of the Braj [?] to blessed Nino, for they had been baptized by her father Zabulon.
And they had heard all this from Jerusalem, Rome and Constantinople: that over that northern land
the Sun of Righteousness had spread, the Light who came from the Father, Christ. And for this reason the blessed letter had been written,
so that they might learn of those deeds and miracles, the wonders of the pillar and of the bramble bush, and the power of healing
that the archdeacon saw, and in amazement he glorified God. And he took the letters and departed.
Chapter 13. On the venerable Cross, which Jacob wrote down. And it came to pass, when that tree of the venerable and victorious, venerable Cross had been cut down,
and ten tens of men carried it upright, with its branches, and they brought it with its leaves into the city.
And the people were amazed at how green and leafy it was in those days at the start of summer, when every other tree was dry,
while this one had all its leaves unwithered, and was fragrant and beautiful to look at. Then they set it up upright on its base at the south door of the church.
And a breeze blew from the waters, passed through the leaves of the tree and stirred its branches.
And its appearance was beautiful and fragrant, as we know by hearsay of the aloe tree. And we cut this down in the month of March, on the 25th, on a Friday.
And that tree stood for thirty-seven days, and its leaves did not change, as though it were standing on its own root at the head of the spring,
until all the trees of the forest were clothed with leaves and the fruit trees were adorned with blossoms.
Then, on the first of the month of May, these crosses were made, and on the seventh of that month they were set up by the laying on of the king's hands,
with joy and great eagerness on the part of the whole city, when they were all in the church.

And on those dark nights the multitude of the city saw it: behold, a cross of fire would come down, crowned with stars, and would stand above the church until dawn, and everyone glorified God for this.
And at dawn, just at daybreak, two stars would come out of it: one would go off to the east and the other to the west,
and the cross itself would go on standing there, shining as before, and little by little it would move away toward the Aragvi and stand on the hill of the rock,
on the upper side, near the spring that the tears of Saint Nino had made to well up, and from there it would rise up to heaven.
The whole multitude of the people saw this salvation of our God many times. Only then did we begin to ask the blessed Nino:
"What is it, that a spark comes out and goes from the east and from the west?" And the saint said to the king and to all the people:
"Send men up onto the high mountains: eastward as far as the mountain of Kakheti, and westward as far as your kingdom reaches.
And when those stars shine forth, let them see where they stop, and there set up these two crosses, as a [?] for all Christians and for the overthrow of the enemy."

And the king did so, and had the summits of the mountains watched continuously for ten days. This was on Friday, as it was just dawning toward Saturday, and the same miracle occurred; it happened just as it always happens.
The next day those from the west came, who had been stationed on the mountains, that is, the mountain of Kvabta-Tavi, and they told the king,
that the star had stopped on the mountains of Tkhoti, had come down to the [?] (ergvi) of Kaspi, had stopped at a certain place, and had slowly vanished from sight.
Likewise the men from the east came and said: "We saw the star coming from here, and it stopped at the village of Bodi in the land of Kakheti."
Then blessed Nino ordered that these two crosses be carried off and that one be set up at Tkhoti, where God had shown the king his power:
"And give the other one to Salome of Ujarma, a true handmaid of Christ, and let her set it up in the city of Ujarma.
And let the village of Bodi not stand against the city of the kings, for that is where the great multitude of the people is.
As for the village of Bodi, we shall see that place pleasing to God for ourselves." And we did just as holy Nino had commanded us.

Then we raised up with human hands this honoured cross of Mtskheta, which had been revealed by signs from heaven, and we went to the foot of that hill, to the spring, and there we spent the night and prayed to God.
And the blessed Saint Nino mingled that spring with tears, and healings and very great miracles took place. And the next day we went up onto that rock.
And blessed Nino came and fell down upon the stones of the hill, and she wept, and so did the king and all the nobles and the whole multitude of the people,
men and women; and there was a wailing of little children, so that even the mountains echoed. And holy Nino laid her hand on one stone and said to me:
"Come, it is fitting for you: draw a cross on this stone." And I did so. And there the kings set up that glorious cross.
And the king bent down on his knees, with all the nobles and the whole multitude of the people, and they bowed down before the cross clothed in victory,
and they confessed the crucified Jesus Christ as truly God and Son of the living God, and they believed in the God of all, glorified in Trinity, to whom glory is fitting forever and ever. Amen.
But the noblewomen never left the holy church, the pillar of light and the life-giving cross, for they saw the immeasurable miracles and the healings past telling.
Then holy Nino left the city of Mtskheta and went to the mountain people to preach to those beast-like men and to smash their idols.
But she left Abiathar here, the priest who had been a Jew. He was a second Paul, and he did not stop preaching Christ and his glory night and day,
until the Jews began to flee. But concerning the shrine, he urged the king not to disturb its buildings, but rather to add to the construction.
For before the new grace had yet appeared in this land, the glorious name of the eternal God was in that place.
And the king [?] in his days, and descendants of Elioz were there as priests over the Jews.
Chapter 14. The raising of the venerable Cross of Mtskheta and then its manifestation again. And it came to pass, when all Kartli had been converted,
The priests who had come from Greece took counsel to set up the sign of the cross. The priests said to King Mirian:
"It is fitting and proper to set up the Lord's sign of the cross." And this seemed good to the king and to all the people.
And they joyfully accepted the word and the teaching of the priests. And King Mirian ordered wood for a cross.
The carpenters went and cut down a lofty tree. And the king ordered a cross to be made.
And the priests taught them the shape of the cross. When the carpenters had made the cross, they came and told King Mirian:
"We have made that Cross, as the priests taught us." And at once the king rose with joy, and all the people saw the form of that Cross.
And they were greatly astonished and glorified God. At that time the king understood and remembered when the day had grown dark on the mountain.
and how he had seen a light of great brilliance in the likeness of a cross; and as soon as he saw it, he recognized it.
Then he told the priests and all the people about that vision, and how the sign of the cross had lit up the darkness before his eyes.
Then, when the people heard the king's words, they believed even more strongly in Jesus Christ and in the sign of his cross,
and all of them together joyfully bowed down before it and glorified God.
Then the king consulted with all the people about where they should set up the form of the cross.
But each person said wherever seemed right to him, and they could not choose any place. At that time King Mirian prayed and said:
"Lord Jesus Christ, in whom we have believed through this captive woman, and whom these priests of yours have taught us, you, Jesus Christ,
who humbled yourself and in your humility put on the form of a servant, who came down from the blessed bosom of the Father,
You who for our sake left thrones, dominions and powers and made your dwelling in the womb of the holy Virgin, and then were crucified under Pilate of Pontus,
were buried in the heart of the earth, and on the third day rose again and fulfilled everything spoken by the prophets, ascended into heaven and sat down at the right hand of the Father,
and will come again to judge the living and the dead, and you left us the sign of your cross to overthrow the invisible devices of the enemy;
and we who fear you have received it as a sign, so that we may escape from the face of the devil, by whom we had been taken captive.
And now, O Lord God our Savior, be pleased to reveal the place where we should raise up the sign of your cross,
so that those who hate us may see it and be ashamed, because you, Lord, have helped us and comforted us."
And when evening came, that night an angel of the Lord stood over King Mirian in a vision and showed him a hill on the far side of the Aragvi, near Mtskheta, and said to him:
"God has chosen this place. Set up the sign of the cross upon it."
And when day dawned, King Mirian told those priests the vision of the angel and also the word that he had spoken to him.
and also the hill that the angel had shown him. When they heard of the vision and saw the place, the hill pleased all the people,
and with joy and great singing all of them together took up the cross and raised the victorious sign of the cross on that hill near Mtskheta,
directly to the east, on Sunday, on the feast of the Completion of Easter.

And when the sign of the cross was raised up in the land of Kartli, at that very moment all the idols that were within the borders of Kartli fell down and were shattered, and the idol temples were destroyed.
When they saw this wonderful deed and the miracle that the victorious sign of the cross had worked against the idols,
they marveled at this deed all the more, and they glorified God and joyfully worshiped the precious cross.
And on that day King Mirian and all the people of Mtskheta made a great offering to the precious cross.
And all Kartli established the feast of the victory-clad Cross at the completion of Easter, the Easter of Easters, on the Lord's Day, until this very day and forever.
And some time later, after Martvili [?], they saw a great and awesome miracle on a Wednesday.
Behold, a pillar of light in the shape of a cross stood above that cross, and twelve angels were crowned around it,
and likewise twelve stars in that same form were crowned around it. And the hill of the cross continually gave off fragrant smoke.
And as they watched that miracle, many of the godless were converted, received baptism, and built churches.
But the faithful were strengthened all the more and glorified God. And then they saw yet another miracle of the honored Cross:
something stood like fire and burned like a flame above the top of the Cross, three times more radiant than the sun,
and just as sparks fly up strongly from a furnace, so it was: angels were going up and coming down upon the precious cross.
Then the hill of the cross rejoiced mightily and the whole earth shook, and a mist of fragrance rose up to heaven from the mountains, hills and valleys,
and the rocks were shattered, and a great fragrance spread over all the land. This did not happen in a single moment or pass quickly; it went on for a long time.
Great voices were heard, and all the people saw it and heard the murmur of hymn-singing;
they were afraid and greatly amazed. With fear and trembling they bowed down before the precious cross and glorified God with great joy.
After some time, as the signs and visions died down, those very great and terrible earthquakes died down as well.
After this, many other signs and wonders came down from heaven upon the precious cross.
All the people saw this, and with fear and trembling they kept coming to bow down eagerly before the precious cross and to glorify God with joy.
At that time there was a certain God-fearing man named Rev, the son of the king. Rev's son was sick and close to death.
For she had only him alone. She took him and laid him before the venerable cross, and with tears she begged of it:
"If you grant me this child, I will build a dome as a dwelling for you."
As he wept bitterly and without ceasing before the precious cross, the child was healed at that very moment. With great joy he took him away, glorifying God and the precious cross.
Afterwards he came to fulfil his vow, and he gave thanks with great rejoicing,
and Rev's son eagerly built the domed chapel of Mtskheta. Every year he would come and perform the service of the precious cross.
From then on, more and more of the sick and infirm came in great numbers. They were healed, and they glorified God and the precious cross with joy.
There was a certain young man whose eyes had both gone blind. He came, fell down before the precious cross and prayed to it earnestly.
After seven days his eyes were opened, and he glorified God and the precious cross with joy.

There was a certain woman who was constantly tormented by an evil spirit, and the torment she suffered was so great that whenever they brought her near the precious cross she would [?] the covering of the cross.
After the fourteenth day the woman was healed. She went away joyfully on her own feet, glorifying God and the precious cross.
There was also another woman who had a son, and the child was suddenly struck dead. His mother lifted him up, brought him and laid him before the precious cross,
and the dead child lay before the holy cross from morning until evening, while the child's mother prayed and wept before the precious cross.
The people standing there said to her: "He is dead. Take him away and bury him, and stop troubling us!"
But she did not give up hope. Instead she wept even more pitifully and begged for help.
Just at evening the child's breath came back to him and he opened his eyes. After three days his mother took him away healed, and she glorified God and the precious cross.
And when everyone saw these glorious miracles of the precious cross,
Many childless people would come and pray to it for children, and once blessed with children they would glorify God and give offerings and thanks to the venerable Cross.
It granted their requests not only to those who went there, but also to those who were far away. If they called on the venerable Cross of Mtskheta in battle or in a struggle,
they would at once overcome their enemies with the help of the venerable Cross, and they would come with great joy to give thanks to the venerable Cross.
Many godless people also fell into distress, but when they called on the venerable Cross of Mtskheta in faith, they were rescued at once,
and they would come with great joy to bow down before the venerable Cross. They would receive baptism, and they would glorify God and the venerable Cross with joy.
Many others fell into great distress and were rescued through prayer to the venerable Cross,
and many who were sick with various diseases would come to pray to the venerable Cross, and they are healed to this very day.
Other miracles also took place before the venerable Cross, sent down from heaven by God, which are not written in this book.
These alone have been written for the praise of God and the glory of the venerable Cross, so that all of us may glorify the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit,
to whom belongs glory, now and always and to the ages of ages. Amen.
Chapter 15. The document that Mirian, king of Kartli, wrote at the time of his death,
He had it written down by the hand of Archbishop Jacob and gave it to Salome of Ujarma, his son's wife, who had true knowledge of everything.
At the time when the Lord remembered this northern land, darkened by sin and full of the Devil's error,
we were like sheep for the slaughter, for I am the thirty-sixth king
Since our fathers lived on down to my own days and devoured their children as sacrifices to loathsome idols, and that innocent people of the land,
Our fathers mowed down their children like hay in order to please the idols,
above all on those two mountains, Armazi and Zaden, whose very stones are soaked with the blood of infants.
Those mountains deserve to be burned up by fire, by the wrath of God.
But when the time came, this blessed woman came, the apostle and evangelist of the Son of God, Saint Nino. At first she came as a captive,
like a foreigner and like a stranger, like one without help, like one deaf and mute, that captive who has now become a queen to us,
the foreigner has become a mother, the helpless one has become a refuge for all, and the one who could not speak has become a powerful preacher who knows the hidden thoughts of my heart.
This holy woman lit the lamp of light in my heart, and even at midnight the shining sun appeared to me: Christ our God, whose light will never fail, forever.
She became our teacher and joined us to the people of Christ through holy baptism and the veneration of the precious Wood.
and she gave us a new law of life and joy, and made us worthy to taste the incorruptible mysteries of heaven.
I became obedient to the commands she taught me, and I built a church for prayer in the garden of my fathers,
And in it is this pillar of light, which I could in no way manage with all human strength and understanding,
but God Most High sent one of his servants, and in an instant it rose from the earth toward heaven.
And your own eyes see its awesomeness and its wonder, and also its healings.
And when he informed me about the setting up of the cross, I sent out carpenters to search for a tree.
And they found a single tree standing alone on a rock, which no human hand had touched;
moreover, we had heard from hunters about the miracle of that tree: when an arrow struck a deer, it would flee to the foot of the hill on which that tree stood,
and would quickly eat the seed of that tree that had fallen to the ground, and would be saved from death. They told me this, and I was amazed at it.
I cut down that tree and made three crosses from it: one is this one, whose sign came from heaven; and one I set up in the place
where I had seen the revelation from the Lord, on the mountain of Tkhoti; and the other one was for the city of Ujarma, and Salome took it there.
And I built a church in Nino's bramble thicket, and in it I made a work both hidden and visible, to the glory of those brambles,
for I did not cut away even a single leaf of them, but enclosed them all around with a framework [?], for I have seen many miracles and great healings there.
And I built the upper church for myself, of stone, with a great multitude of people,
for the lower church was called the "Holy of Holies," and I never dared to open its doors except on Sunday (the Lord's day),
nor did anyone dare to enter except the priests who chant in it, for great fear of that living pillar had fallen on everyone.
And everyone regarded that pillar as the power of God. And people could not even look at its covering [?], which we ourselves see.
And I did not dare to dig earth for my grave in front of it, so that my body might be laid before it, for I was afraid of it, since I had done nothing but sin.
And I prepared my grave higher up, so that I might keep out of its sight and receive its mercy at the resurrection.
And as I was preparing myself for the fulfilment of God's good things upon me, I was saying:
"I will commend my soul to my holy mother Nino." But that holy woman commended her own spotless soul into the hands of her Creator,
for she had fulfilled every commandment of God and the teaching of that holy man, her mother's brother, our father the patriarch; and she left us orphans, newborn and ignorant infants.
And I trembled greatly in my spirit, and the whole race of the north was filled with grief, for the sun of righteousness had only just fully risen and the true [?] had only just spread forth.
And a cloud covered holy Nino. But that holy woman is wholly in light and gives light to us all.
And I resolved with great zeal to bring her holy body here, before the pillar clothed in light, but I found no way at all to do so,
for two hundred men could not move the small bed on which the holy and blessed Nino had come to rest.
Then we buried the holy body of that all-glorious woman at Bodbe, a village in Kakheti.
And we mourned our orphanhood for thirty days, together with my whole royal household. And I built a church over it and greatly honoured it,
And through her intercession I have hope from the Son of God, and in the faith in God the Father without beginning, and the almighty Son, and the life-giving, immortal Holy Spirit.
And I seek and await the resurrection from the dead, and I commend my soul to Christ the King, to whom belong glory, strength and power, now and always and unto ages of ages. Amen."
The testament of King Mirian to his son Rev and his wife Nana. Behold, I am going back to where I came from; but you, Nana,
if you are granted time to live after me, divide my royal treasury in two and take a part to the fasting-place of Saint Nino, on account of the changes of the times,
so that that place may never be shaken, for it is not a seat of kings; that place is poor.
Likewise I entreat the archbishop to establish the glory of that place, for it is worthy of honor.
And he instructed his son: "Behold, our darkness has been changed into light, and our death into life.
Now, wherever you find in your land those afflictions of Kartli, the deceiving idols, burn them with fire, and make whoever mourns them drink their ashes!
And command this to your children, for I know it: in the Caucasus they will not be quickly destroyed. But you, do this:

Commend yourself to that pillar glorified from on high and to the precious cross revealed in the heavens, and may your going into the earth be an eternal sleep in the faith of the Holy Trinity. Amen."
